evals.prompt: We built a study-group app for college students. Nobody uses it. We're at 3 universities.
evals.expected_output: Should identify that spreading across 3 universities is the error: a study app needs local density. Should recommend collapsing to ONE campus, ideally one dorm or one course, until saturation. Should cite Facebook's Harvard-first containment and Graham's fire metaphor. Should recommend in-person recruiting through an existing convener, citing Tinder's sorority tour.
assertions: Recommends narrowing to one campus or smaller unit
Recommends in-person recruiting through an existing group
Names the hard side for this network

evals.prompt: Should I build a waitlist before launching?
evals.expected_output: Should give a conditional answer, not a yes. Waitlists are correct when you need positioning and control over composition (Superhuman hand-picked founders and VCs to seed target networks; 180k waited at $30/mo). They are wrong when you need learning: Figma ran a closed beta and later said they regretted it because it slowed feedback velocity. Should ask which the user needs.
assertions: Does not give an unconditional yes or no
Cites Superhuman as the case for gating
Cites Figma regretting the closed beta as the case against
Frames the decision as positioning versus learning speed
